s24.question: Between November 2025 and February 2026, porosity went up across several people's trials even though nobody changed their recipes. What changed? Cite the evidence.
s24.answer:
The notebook points to a equipment change, not a recipe change. From 2025-11-03, several trials were mixed on "Planetary mixer #2 (loaner unit)" instead of the primary "Planetary mixer," and none of those trials logged a degas step [T677], [T678], [T682], [T687]. The loaner was still in use on 2026-02-09 [T773].

| Evidence | Trials | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Loaner mixer from Nov | [T677], [T678], [T682] | "Planetary mixer #2 (loaner unit)" |
| Primary mixer before | [T671] | "Planetary mixer," porosity 2.99% |
| Degassed on same loaner | [T679] vs [T678] | 0.33% passed; 1.67% failed |
| Rest time not the cause | [T677], [T678] | 0.4 h and 0.7 h both failed |
| Group by degassing | all trials | degassed mean 0.93%; not degassed 1.17% |

Hypothesis: The loaner mixer may trap more air, and skipping degassing may leave those bubbles in the cured part. Resin this brittle is flaw-sensitive, so a bubble may start a crack. Ines's 10-minute degas [T679] passed on the same loaner, which fits this, and it is her habit of degassing that stands out.

Uncertain: I checked six trials across Dana, Ravi and Ines. The notebook doesn't record what the loaner does differently, and [T671] already had high porosity on the primary mixer, so the mixer may not be the whole story. Degassing is not in SOP v1 [T679], and the group gap is small, so this needs a controlled test.

I haven't filed anything. The open question [L10] and the group finding [L14] are the places this belongs.

s25.question: T541 (Ravi Menon) and T586 (Lucia Ferreira) used the same recipe, but T586 came out with much lower porosity. What explains the difference? Cite the evidence.
s25.answer:
The notebook shows no logged process difference between [T541] and [T586]. Both used 34% diluent, 1.4% photoinitiator, no degas, a 0.6 h rest, 3000 rpm for 2 min, and 45 min post-cure [T541-L02], [T586-L02], [T541-L05], [T586-L05]. The only difference is a free-text note on [T586-N2]: Lucia warmed the resin to 40 °C for 20 min before loading the vat, "as I always do." Porosity was 0.67% for [T586] and 2.08% for [T541], which failed the porosity guardrail [T541-N2]. Viscosity was similar (1.44 vs 1.4 Pa·s), and both passed tensile.

Hypothesis: Lucia's warm-up habit may let trapped air escape before printing, so fewer bubbles remain to act as cracks in this brittle resin. Degassing on the same recipe also cut porosity: [T887] with a 10-min vacuum degas reached 0.23% [T887-L06].

Uncertain: this rests on one pair of trials and one unlogged note. The warm-up is not in the device log, and its note is timestamped 13:44 [T586-N2], after the print job started at 12:14 [T586-L07], so I can't confirm when it happened. My group comparison of Lucia's trials at this recipe failed on an owner-filter error, so I have no cross-trial check of warming.

s26.question: What is the median porosity across all 1000 trials (excluded ones included)?
s26.answer: The notebook has no median figure, and I can't derive one from the tool outputs without computing a new number. The compare tool returned per-trial porosity for both groups, which together cover all 1000 trials. Excluded trials (n=21) have a mean of 1.34, ranging from 0.06 [T568] to 4.43 [T775], and 10 of 21 passed every guardrail. Included trials (n=979) have a mean of 1.12, ranging from 0.1 [T848] to 9.14 [T687], and 584 of 979 passed every guardrail. The porosity guardrail is 1% or less, so the mean sits above that limit in both groups even though most trials pass. Getting the true median would need a median option added to the compare tool, or someone to sort the 1000 values directly.
